title: "nososim: minimal validation"
format: html
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false

Three questions: **Does $R$ give the expected offspring distribution? Does mixing give the expected assortativity? Do interventions reduce transmission?**

## Scenarios

Define each family once, varying only $R$, within-group mixing, or IPC intervention. Each scenario uses 200 replicates; mixing scenarios start with eight cases per group.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(linktree)
library(furrr)
#devtools::install()
library(nososim)
library(pipetime)
n_rep <- 200

scenario <- function(
  type,
  R = 2,
  n = 200,
  days = 25,
  w = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3),
  mixing = NULL,
  seeds = 1,
  reduction = 0,
  from = Inf
) {
  list(
    type = type,
    R = R,
    n = n,
    days = days,
    w = w,
    mixing = mixing,
    seeds = seeds,
    reduction = reduction,
    from = from
  )
}

mix <- function(within) {
  matrix(
    c(within, 1, 1, within),
    2,
    byrow = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(c("A", "B"), c("A", "B"))
  )
}

scenarios <- c(
  set_names(0:3, paste0("R", 0:3)) |>
    map(\(R) scenario("offspring", R = R, days = 1, w = 1)),
  c(disassortative = 0.5, random = 1, assortative = 4) |>
    map(\(within) {
      scenario(
        "mixing",
        R = 3,
        n = 300,
        days = 1,
        w = 1,
        seeds = 8,
        mixing = mix(within)
      )
    }),
  c(no_control = 0, half_control = 0.5, full_control = 1) |>
    map(\(reduction) {
      scenario("control", R = 3, from = 8, reduction = reduction)
    })
)

design <- tibble(
  name = names(scenarios),
  type = map_chr(scenarios, "type"),
  spec = unname(scenarios)
)
```

## Simulation

Use the same simulation for every scenario: create the population, seed infections, then apply mixing and controls. A fixed seed for each run makes results reproducible.

```{r}
simulate <- function(s, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  dates <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:s$days

  timeline <- make_timeline(
    n = s$n,
    dates = dates,
    stay = s$days + 1,
    R = s$R,
    attributes = if (is.null(s$mixing)) {
      list()
    } else {
      list(group = c(A = 0.5, B = 0.5))
    }
  )

  people <- distinct(timeline, id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  imported <- if (is.null(s$mixing)) {
    slice_head(people, n = s$seeds)
  } else {
    people |> group_by(group) |> slice_head(n = s$seeds) |> ungroup()
  }
  imported <- transmute(imported, id, date = dates[1])

  intervention <- function(present, date) {
    value <- if (as.integer(date - dates[1]) >= s$from) s$reduction else 0
    matrix(
      value,
      nrow(present),
      nrow(present),
      dimnames = list(present$id, present$id)
    )
  }

  make_outbreak(
    timeline,
    imported,
    w = s$w,
    dates = dates,
    intervention = intervention,
    mixing = if (is.null(s$mixing)) NULL else list(group = s$mixing)
  )
}

future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 5)

runs <- expand_grid(design, replicate = seq_len(n_rep)) |>
  mutate(
    seed = 1000L + row_number(),
    outbreak = furrr::future_map2(
      spec,
      seed,
      simulate,
      .options = furrr::furrr_options(seed = TRUE)
    )
  ) |>
  time_pipe("runs")

future::plan(future::sequential) # Close workers when finished
```

## Outputs

Summarise total cases for every run, then extract the relevant measure for each family: imported-case offspring, group assortativity, or daily incidence (including zero-case days).

```{r}
get_summary <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    cases = nrow(x$infections),
    attack_rate = nrow(x$infections) / n_distinct(x$timeline$id)
  )
}

get_offspring <- function(x) {
  # Only imported cases have complete follow-up in the one-day benchmark.
  nososim::offspring(x) |>
    semi_join(x$parameters$imported, by = "id")
}

get_incidence <- function(x) {
  counts <- x$infections |>
    mutate(day = as.integer(date_infection - min(x$dates))) |>
    count(day, name = "cases")
  tibble(day = seq_along(x$dates) - 1L) |>
    left_join(counts, by = "day") |>
    mutate(cases = replace_na(cases, 0L))
}

get_assortativity <- function(x, s) {
  groups <- distinct(x$timeline, id, group)
  edges <- nososim::count_edges(x, by = "group") |>
    uncount(transmissions) |>
    rename(from = source_group, to = recipient_group)

  sizes <- count(groups, group)
  f <- setNames(sizes$n, sizes$group)
  estimates <- if (n_distinct(c(edges$from, edges$to)) < 2) {
    tibble(group = character(), est = double(), lwr = double(), upr = double())
  } else {
    as_tibble(linktree::get_delta(edges$from, edges$to, f = f))
  }

  M <- s$mixing
  tibble(
    group = rownames(M),
    expected = linktree::gamma2delta(diag(M) / c(M[1, 2], M[2, 1]))
  ) |>
    left_join(estimates, by = "group")
}

# Keep run identifiers and unnest each measure in one shared pipeline.
collect_measure <- function(data, measure) {
  data |>
    transmute(name, replicate, data = map2(outbreak, spec, measure)) |>
    unnest(data)
}

by_type <- split(runs, runs$type)
outbreak_summary <- collect_measure(runs, \(x, s) get_summary(x))
offspring <- collect_measure(by_type$offspring, \(x, s) get_offspring(x))
assortativity <- collect_measure(by_type$mixing, get_assortativity)
incidence <- collect_measure(by_type$control, \(x, s) get_incidence(x))
```

## Checks and figures

**1. Offspring: observed versus exact expectation**

With one imported case and one day generation time, offspring follow a binomial distribution. Compare the simulated mean with its exact expectation, allowing three Monte Carlo standard errors.

```{r}
offspring_theory <- design |>
  filter(type == "offspring") |>
  transmute(name, R = map_dbl(spec, "R"), n = map_dbl(spec, "n")) |>
  mutate(
    susceptible = n - 1,
    p = 1 - exp(-R / susceptible),
    expected = susceptible * p,
    mc_se = sqrt(susceptible * p * (1 - p) / n_rep)
  )

benchmarks <- offspring_theory |>
  left_join(
    offspring |>
      group_by(name) |>
      summarise(observed = mean(offspring), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "name"
  ) |>
  mutate(pass = abs(observed - expected) <= 3 * mc_se)
benchmarks

reference <- offspring_theory |>
  transmute(
    name,
    data = map2(susceptible, p, \(size, prob) {
      k <- 0:12
      tibble(offspring = k, p = dbinom(k, size, prob))
    })
  ) |>
  unnest(data)

p_offspring <- offspring |>
  count(name, offspring) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  mutate(p = n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(offspring, p)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_point(data = reference, aes(offspring, p), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~name) +
  labs(x = "Secondary infections per imported case", y = "Probability") +
  theme_classic()
p_offspring
```

**2. Mixing: observed versus theoretical `linktree` assortativity**

Compare estimated assortativity with the value implied by each mixing matrix. The dashed identity line shows agreement; larger squares show replicate means.

```{r}
assortativity |>
  group_by(name, group, expected) |>
  summarise(estimated = mean(est, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

p_assortativity <- ggplot(assortativity, aes(expected, est, colour = group)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3, shape = 15) +
  labs(x = "Expected delta from mixing matrix", y = "Estimated delta") +
  theme_classic()
p_assortativity
```

**3. Interventions: incidence and attack rate**

Compare daily infections and final attack rates across control strengths. Complete control must prevent all new infections from its start day onward.

```{r}
controls <- design |>
  filter(type == "control") |>
  transmute(
    name,
    from = map_dbl(spec, "from"),
    reduction = map_dbl(spec, "reduction")
  )

outbreak_summary |>
  semi_join(controls, by = "name") |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(mean_attack_rate = mean(attack_rate), .groups = "drop")

p_control <- incidence |>
  group_by(name, day) |>
  summarise(
    mean_cases = mean(cases),
    .groups = "drop",
    lwr = quantile(cases, 0.025),
    upr = quantile(cases, 0.975)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, mean_cases, group = name)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, fill = name), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = name)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = name)) +
  geom_vline(
    data = distinct(controls, from),
    aes(xintercept = from),
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Mean daily infections", colour = "Intervention") +
  theme_classic()
p_control
```

Expected outcomes: offspring means match the binomial formula within Monte Carlo error; early assortativity increases with within-group mixing and approximately matches the identity line; stronger controls reduce incidence and final attack rate, with no new infections from the start of complete control. 

## Add a scenario: block ward A → ward B

From `ipc_start` (inclusive), block only A → B transmissions.

```{r}
ward_dates <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:25
ipc_start <- ward_dates[1] + 5

block_A_to_B <- function(present, date) {
  E <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow(present),
    nrow(present),
    dimnames = list(present$id, present$id)
  )
  if (date >= ipc_start) {
    E[present$ward == "A", present$ward == "B"] <- 1
  }
  E
}

simulate_wards <- function(seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  timeline <- make_timeline(
    n = 300,
    dates = ward_dates,
    stay = length(ward_dates),
    R = 2,
    attributes = list(ward = c(A = 0.5, B = 0.5))
  )
  imported <- timeline |>
    distinct(id, ward) |>
    group_by(ward) |>
    slice_head(n = 4) |>
    ungroup() |>
    transmute(id, date = ward_dates[1])

  make_outbreak(
    timeline,
    imported,
    w = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3),
    dates = ward_dates,
    intervention = block_A_to_B
  )
}

ward_runs <- tibble(replicate = seq_len(n_rep)) |>
  mutate(outbreak = map(2025L + replicate, simulate_wards))
```

Use `count_edges(by_date = TRUE)` to count each route by infection date. Fill absent routes and dates with zeros within every replicate, so means include runs with no transmission.

```{r}
ward_daily <- ward_runs |>
  transmute(
    replicate,
    data = map(outbreak, \(x) {
      nososim::count_edges(x, by = "ward", by_date = TRUE) |>
        complete(
          date_infection = ward_dates,
          source_ward = c("A", "B"),
          recipient_ward = c("A", "B"),
          fill = list(transmissions = 0L)
        )
    })
  ) |>
  unnest(data) |>
  mutate(route = paste(source_ward, "→", recipient_ward))

ward_results <- ward_daily |>
  mutate(
    period = if_else(date_infection < ipc_start, "Before IPC", "From IPC start")
  ) |>
  group_by(replicate, route, period) |>
  summarise(transmissions = sum(transmissions), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(route, period) |>
  summarise(mean_transmissions = mean(transmissions), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = mean_transmissions)
ward_results

ward_daily_summary <- ward_daily |>
  group_by(date_infection, route) |>
  summarise(
    mean_transmissions = mean(transmissions),
    lower = quantile(transmissions, 0.025),
    upper = quantile(transmissions, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ward_daily_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(date_infection, mean_transmissions)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ipc_start, colour = "orange") +
  facet_wrap(~route) +
  labs(
    x = "Infection date",
    y = "transmission count"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
